title: Tidal energy plans and sea-space limits in Singapore
asked: Dr Neo Kok Beng asked what the Government's plan or strategy is for tidal energy, and what maritime constraints prevent scaling hydrokinetic turbine arrays in the Singapore Strait, citing a March 2026 NUS study that tidal energy could meet about 22% of Singapore's electricity demand.
response: Ms Gan Siow Huang said studies on deploying tidal energy in Singapore have been done, but there are no current plans to deploy it. Sea space is limited because much of Singapore's territorial waters is already used for ports, anchorage and shipping lanes. She said the NUS study cited did not take into account these existing uses of sea space or the cost-effectiveness of tidal energy, and that the amount realistically harnessable domestically is estimated at less than 1% of Singapore's energy needs.
